model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, perpetual-bond and preference-share coupons and NCI charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net operating income, RMB m, on the CSV's consistent series: H1 2026 actual 174,762 (+3.87% YoY) + H2 2026E ~169,300 (FY2025 H2 actual 163,549 x 1.035). FY2025 actual 331,800; FY2024 334,489; FY2023 336,602 - three flat years, the first growth since FY2022 arriving in H1 2026 as deposit repricing finally outran asset-yield decline (NII +5.6% YoY, fees +6.0%). Operating income = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other net non-interest income.
inputs.share_count_basis: 25,219,845,601 ordinary shares (A 20,628,944,429 + H 4,590,901,172, one class, same economic rights). Weighted average = basic = diluted 25,220m every year FY2018-FY2025 (FY2025 annual line 10856). Held FLAT: no share scheme, no convertible, no buyback; the RMB27.5bn preference shares were redeemed in Q1 2026 and the perpetual bonds are non-convertible, so neither dilutes. CMB has not issued ordinary equity since the 2013 rights issue.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB10.24tn at 30 Jun 2026), borrowings from the central bank (RMB140bn at FY2025), interbank funding and debt securities issued are operating funding, and cash/central-bank balances (RMB840bn) are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows. The CSV's total_debt column (143,487 at FY2025, i.e. debt securities issued) is NOT used.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE at a constant 14.0% CET1 ratio: net profit to ORDINARY shareholders ~146bn (PBT ~182.6bn x (1 - 20%) for tax ~15.5%, NCI ~0.5%, perpetual/preference coupons ~3%) LESS the equity retained to hold CET1 at 14.0% on FY2026E RWA ~8,165bn versus FY2025 net CET1 1,067,560 (0.14 x 8,165,000 - 1,067,560 = 75,540), i.e. ~70bn before the ~18bn/yr OCI and regulatory-deduction leakage seen in FY2025 (ordinary equity +49.9bn vs retained profit ~68bn), so ~50bn net - roughly the FY2025 cash dividend (50,767). FY2025 on the same basis: NI to ordinary 143,874 less 0.1416 x RWA growth 654bn = 92.6bn gives FCFE ~51bn = the dividend, which is exactly why the CET1 ratio slipped 14.86% -> 14.16% while paying out 35%. Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: 451,457 - 28,141 = 423bn) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: the 'Share-based payment' line in the FY2018-FY2025 statements of changes in equity (e.g. FY2025 annual line 15299, nil) is the legacy H-share appreciation rights plan, a cash-settled liability, not equity dilution; no option or employee share scheme, basic = diluted EPS (RMB5.70 FY2025), no repurchases. House and street bases coincide; band_position is null.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1750 at 2026-10-23T08:47Z, Yahoo Finance. Triangulated against USDCNY=X 6.6699 / USDHKD=X 7.8407 = 1.1755 (same source, same day). Parity check: the Shanghai A share (600036.SS) closed at CNY 41.77 = HKD 49.08 on the same day, so the H share trades at a ~5% PREMIUM to the A share - unusual for Chinese banks (most H shares trade at a 20-30% discount) and a sign the H line is already the fully-valued one. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares; H-share dividends are declared in RMB and paid in HKD at the PBOC rate.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.cet1_anchor: Group, Advanced Approach (the headline measure): CET1 ratio 14.07% = net CET1 1,115,273 on RWA 7,928,939 at 30 Jun 2026 (interim lines 1391-1401); 14.16% = 1,067,560 on 7,540,202 at FY2025 (annual lines 1850-1861); 14.86% = 1,023,048 on ~6,885,800 at FY2024. The FY2023 -> FY2024 step 13.73% -> 14.86% is the new PRC capital rules (effective 1 Jan 2024), not organic build. Under the Weighted Approach the ratio is 11.92% on RWA 8,954bn (FY2025, line 1937) vs a D-SIB minimum of ~8.25%: ~3.7pt of buffer even on the stricter measure. RWA +9.5% in FY2025 and +5.2% in H1 2026 alone against loan growth of ~6%: market-risk RWA +62% in FY2025 under the new rules.
inputs.payout_anchor: FY2025 cash dividend RMB2.016/share (interim 1.013 paid Jan 2026 + final 1.003 paid Jul 2026) = RMB50.8bn = 35.3% of NI to ordinary shareholders; payout held at or above 35% since 2023 and above 30% since 2013; first interim dividend introduced in 2025 and continued for 2026 (interim line 3866). Perpetual/preference coupons FY2025: 996 + 5,311 = 6,307 (annual lines 8936-8937); preference shares (RMB27.5bn) redeemed Q1 2026, RMB50bn new perpetual bonds issued Q2 2026 (OtherEquityInstruments 177,457 -> 149,989 -> 199,989).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% for CNY-denominated flows: 10-year CGB ~1.8% + China equity risk premium ~6.5% x beta ~1.0 = ~8.3%, plus ~1.7pt for H-share governance/capital-controls/policy-lending risk. Set 0.5pt BELOW the 10.5% used for 0998.HK (CITIC) and 3618.HK (CQRCB) and 1pt below 2016.HK (Zheshang): CMB has the sector's highest ROE (13.4% vs 8-10%), lowest NPL (0.94%), highest coverage (385%), thickest CET1 (14.1%) and the largest fee franchise (RMB18tn retail AUM), so it deserves the lowest CoE of the Chinese bank set, but a Chinese bank H-share should not be discounted below 10%. Bear 10.5%, bull 9.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 lease liabilities (RMB11.3bn at FY2025) sit inside operating funding; the depreciation and interest on right-of-use assets are already inside operating expenses and PBT, so no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path 0).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (RMB8.3bn of equity, 945m of FY2025 profit = 0.5% of PBT) and are charged inside cash_tax_rate_path together with the perpetual-bond coupons, so the flow is to ORDINARY shareholders. Nothing is deducted after the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the component engine so the dashboard sliders work: revenue = net operating income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax margin after credit impairment (D&A, SBC, leases zero); cash_tax_rate_path = income tax + NCI + perpetual/preference coupons as a share of PBT, so NOPAT = net profit to ordinary shareholders; capex_pct_path = equity retained to hold the CET1 ratio on RWA growth; wc_capture 0; net debt 0 and nothing bridged (deposits are not debt, and the flow is already post-interest, so EV = equity value). Residual-income cross-check: FY2026E ordinary BVPS ~RMB46.5 x (ROE 13% - g 3%)/(CoE 10% - 3%) = 1.43x book = RMB66 = HKD78 at a constant ROE; the FCFE model is lower because it charges the capital that 7%->3% RWA growth consumes and lets NI/RWA keep drifting down (terminal ROE on CET1 ~10.7%, terminal P/B on CET1 ~1.1x). Fresh build 2026-10-23: no prior DCF or Drivers file; the 3618.HK memory line references this ticker only as a wrong-company warning.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward FY2027E operating-income growth (base case year 1), anchored on H1 2026 +3.9% YoY and FY2026 loan/deposit guidance of 6-7%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary equity CAGR (9.9% 3yr / 11.4% 5yr) is 3-10x the revenue CAGR (-1.0% / 2.9%) and well above net income (2.9% / 9.1%): the book is compounding from a 65% retention ratio on RWA growth, not from earnings growth, and ROE has fallen from 17.1% (FY2022) to 13.4% (FY2025). The equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue is net operating income (CSV series). EPS FY2020 3.79 -> FY2025 5.70 (RMB). Ordinary shareholders' equity FY2020 639,696 -> FY2025 1,095,420; BVPS 25.36 -> 43.43. Reported FCF for a bank is deposit-flow noise (FY2022 +535bn, FY2019 -20bn), so no FCF CAGR is computed; the FCFE series used in the model is constructed from net profit less CET1 retention and is ~flat at ~50bn FY2024-FY2026E.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +4% in FY2027-28 fading to 3%: loans/deposits +6-7% (FY2026 guidance), NIM drifting from 1.83% (H1 2026) to ~1.7% and then flat as deposit repricing catches up (NII already +5.6% YoY in H1 2026), wealth-management fees +10-15% on RMB18tn AUM, other non-interest income (trading/FX) flat. Below RWA growth every year, so NI/RWA keeps declining as the mix shifts and NIM stays low.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment: FY2023 52.5%, FY2024 53.4%, FY2025 53.9%, FY2026E ~53.1% (H1 2026 51.9% vs 52.8% a year earlier as impairment rose 18% YoY to 29.2bn on retail/credit-card NPLs). Base eases to 51%: credit cost normalises up from the FY2024-25 low (~40bn/yr, 0.55% of loans, vs 65bn in FY2021), cost-to-income held ~32% by AI/digitisation. The 385% provision coverage (RMB260bn+ of allowances against RMB70bn of NPLs) is a cushion the model does not release.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 14.0% (Advanced Approach; FY2026E ~14.0%) on RWA growth of 7.0, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0% from FY2026E RWA RMB8,165bn (FY2025 7,540bn; H1 2026 7,929bn) and FY2026E net CET1 ~1,140bn. FY2027 retention 83.1bn = 0.14 x 8,736.6bn - 1,140bn; converging on 0.03 x 0.14 x prior RWA = 53bn in FY2036 (11.1% of income). Terminal-year CET1 ~RMB1,825bn on RWA 13,038bn; terminal ROE on CET1 ~10.7%. No release of the 14% buffer toward the ~8.25% minimum: management guides to keeping capital at a 'relatively outstanding level' and has never bought back stock.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~15.5% of PBT (FY2025 15.6%, FY2024 16.3%, H1 2026 15.2% - below the 25% statutory rate because of tax-exempt government-bond and fund income) + NCI ~0.5% + perpetual-bond coupons ~5.5-6bn ~3.2% of PBT (FY2025: 996 + 5,311 = 6,307 = 3.5%; preference shares redeemed Q1 2026 but RMB50bn of new perpetuals issued Q2 2026) = ~19.5%, set at 20% flat to allow the tax-exempt share to shrink. Coupons are fixed in RMB so their share falls as PBT grows; ignored (conservative). Check: FY2025 NI to ordinary 143,874 / PBT 178,993 = 80.4%.
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 10.0% - 3.0% = 14.3x; the 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B on CET1 ~1.1x at terminal ROE ~10.7%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (10.7 - 3)/(10 - 3).
base.narrative: Steady-state premium Chinese bank: NIM bottoms ~1.7%, credit cost normalises modestly, wealth fees keep growing, RWA growth decelerates from 7% to 3% and CET1 is held at 14%. FCFE ~RMB67bn in FY2027 (covering the ~52bn dividend with room) rising to ~142bn by FY2036 as retention falls.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM stabilises at ~1.8% in FY2027 as deposit costs reprice faster than LPR (H1 2026 already showed NII +5.6%), wealth-management fees compound at 15%+ (H1 2026 +18.4%) on AUM growing double digits, capital-market recovery lifts other non-interest income; loan growth 7%.
bull.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin holds at the FY2024-25 level (53.4-53.9%): credit cost stays ~0.55% of loans as property and retail NPLs stabilise, coverage allowed to drift from 385% toward 350% (a modest release the base denies), cost-to-income improves toward 30% on AI.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 target glides 14.0% -> 13.5% over five years (a 0.5pt release, ~RMB50bn, funding a higher payout or a first buyback) on RWA growth of 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0% as capital-light wealth income takes share of growth. Terminal RWA 12,550bn, CET1 ~1,694bn.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% - 3.5% = 16.7x; the 18x cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: The retail-and-wealth franchise re-rates: NIM troughs, fee income becomes 25%+ of revenue, ROE holds ~13%, and capital is partly returned. FCFE ~RMB88bn in FY2027 rising to ~174bn by FY2036.

bear.growth_rationale: Further PBOC/LPR cuts take NIM to ~1.6% by FY2028 (another -20bp, the FY2023-25 pace continuing), household deleveraging keeps retail loans flat, wealth fee growth slows to mid-single digits on weak capital markets; operating income roughly flat for two more years then grows 2-2.5%.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises to ~0.75% of loans (impairment ~55-60bn, back toward the FY2019-22 level) as retail/credit-card NPLs (1.06% and rising), property-development NPLs (4.78%) and LGFV resolution bite, while cost-to-income rises toward 34% on flat revenue. Pre-tax margin back to the FY2020-21 range (~43-45% was pre-impairment-release; 48% here).
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed lending keeps RWA growing 8, 7, 6, 5.5, 5, 4.5, 4, 4, 3.5, 3.5% while earnings stall, so CET1 at 14.0% absorbs a larger share of a smaller profit: FY2027 retention 94.5bn (27% of income) vs net profit ~142bn, leaving FCFE ~47bn, below the ~52bn dividend - the FY2025 pattern (ratio drift funding the payout) persists.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.5% - 2.5% = 12.5x; the 18x cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: Japanification-lite: NIM 1.6%, credit cost up, revenue flat for two years, RWA still growing on policy lending. FCFE dips below the dividend in FY2027-28 and recovers only as RWA growth slows; terminal ROE on CET1 ~8.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: CMB remains China's best-run bank but earns it in a 1.7% NIM world. Operating income grows 3-4% (NII mid-single digits on 6-7% loan growth and stabilising deposit costs; wealth fees double digits), the pre-tax margin eases ~3pt as credit cost normalises from a cyclical low, and the 14% CET1 ratio is held on RWA growth that decelerates from 7% to 3%. Net profit to ordinary shareholders ~RMB150bn in FY2027 funds ~83bn of retention and ~67bn of FCFE, covering the 35% payout with room; by FY2036 retention halves and FCFE rises to ~140bn. Terminal P/B on CET1 ~1.1x at a ~10.7% ROE.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM troughs at ~1.8% in FY2027 as deposit repricing catches up, wealth-management fees compound 15%+ on RMB18tn+ AUM, credit cost stays at the FY2024-25 low and coverage is allowed to drift down from 385%. ROE holds ~13%, CET1 is glided to 13.5% and the surplus returned. The H-share already trades at a premium to the A-share, so the re-rating is in earnings and payout, not multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Another leg of LPR cuts takes NIM to 1.6%, household deleveraging flattens retail lending, credit-card and property NPLs push impairments back toward 55-60bn, and policy lending keeps RWA growing 7-8% against flat earnings. FCFE falls below the dividend for two years and the CET1 ratio drifts down to fund it - the FY2025 pattern, extended. Terminal ROE on CET1 ~8.5%, P/B ~0.75x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the house default 15%, below the 30-35% used for 0998.HK/CITIC and 3618.HK/CQRCB): CMB's capital (CET1 14.1%, ~6pt above its minimum on the Advanced Approach, ~3.7pt on the Weighted), asset quality (NPL 0.94%, coverage 385%) and a decade of ROE >13% argue for materially less downside weight than other Chinese banks, but the structural NIM decline (2.59% -> 1.83% in seven years), rising retail/credit-card NPLs, the property and LGFV tail and the China policy/capital-controls overhang on an H-share argue for well above the default. Bull 25% (above peers' 15-20%): CMB is the one Chinese bank with a genuine capital-light growth engine (wealth fees +18% in H1 2026) and NII inflected positive in H1 2026 for the first time since FY2022. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the cash it can pay its ordinary shareholders after funding the capital its balance sheet growth requires, discounted at the cost of equity - not on reported operating cash flow, which for CMB is deposit-flow noise of +/-RMB500bn a year. The flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI and perpetual/preference coupons) less the CET1 retained on RWA growth at a constant 14% ratio; no capital release is assumed because management has never bought back stock and guides to keeping capital 'relatively outstanding'. The model deliberately lets NI/RWA keep drifting down (revenue grows slower than RWA in every year of every scenario), which is the central fact of Chinese banking in a 1.8% NIM world; the offset CMB uniquely has is a 36% non-interest share led by wealth fees growing double digits. Deposits are not debt and nothing is bridged after the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM: every 10bp on ~RMB12tn of interest-earning assets is ~RMB12bn of pre-tax profit, ~7% of PBT; the base assumes a trough at ~1.7%, the bear 1.6%, and a further easing cycle could take it lower
Credit cost: impairments at 0.55% of loans are at a cyclical low with coverage of 385%; a return to the FY2019-22 charge (~RMB60-65bn) is worth ~RMB20bn of PBT, ~11%

RWA growth versus earnings: the CET1 ratio slipped 0.7pt in FY2025 at 9.5% RWA growth; if policy lending keeps RWA growing faster than ~7%, FCFE falls below the dividend and the 14% ratio cannot be held without a cut or a capital raise
Cost of equity: at 10% the base IV is ~HKD65; at 11% it is ~HKD56 and at 12% ~HKD49 (see the required-return table) - the valuation is a bet on CMB deserving a lower CoE than other Chinese banks
H-share premium to A-share (~5%) and CNY/HKD: the H line has no discount cushion, and a 5% RMB depreciation takes 5% off the HKD value directly
Management transition (new President April 2026) and the regulatory/policy environment (anti-involution pricing, LGFV resolution, dividend and capital directives) are outside the model

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range HKD 43.34-54.25; CNYHKD and the 600036.SS A-share cross from the same source at the same time
data_sources.financials: 3968.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2018-FY2025 annual reports, H1 2024-H1 2026 interim reports, Q1/Q3 quarterly reports; IFRS, RMB millions); capital adequacy, RWA, dividend and coupon lines from 3968.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt and 3968.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt as cited in inputs
data_sources.qualitative: 3968.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23): business model, moat, risks, FY2026 guidance (loans/deposits +6-7%, continued NIM pressure), H1 2026 results commentary
